subject: Embedding baseline + packaging: vector size pricing & model eligibility
messages:
From: Emma Lowe <emma@dataforge.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Question on embeddings pricing and supported dims

Hi Markus,

We’re evaluating Redwood for a search/semantic layer in our product. A couple of quick questions to help us model costs for an MVP:

- Do you charge embeddings per-vector or per-token? We have mixed documents (short notes ~60 tokens and long docs ~2k tokens).
- How do you handle dimensionality? Is there a price difference for 1536 vs 4096-dim vectors?
- Which hosted embedding models are supported today — can we choose different models per route?

We expect ~20M embeddings/month in the first 6 months and will likely commit to a quarterly prepay if the unit economics work. Any baseline rate card or example cost calc would be hugely helpful.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Emma
Emma Lowe
Head of Data Products, DataForge
emma@dataforge.com
+44 7700 900123
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@dataforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question on embeddings pricing and supported dims

Thanks for the clear questions, Emma — great to hear about the planned volume. Below is a concise baseline and then some notes on options.

Baseline (hosted API)
- Billing unit: per-vector (embeddings call) rather than per-token; we price per generated vector.
- Unit rates (example baseline, no commitments):
  • 1536-dim model (rwd-embed-1): $0.0006 per vector
  • 4096-dim model (rwd-embed-large): $0.0018 per vector
- Charges are per returned vector; token-size of the source is irrelevant for base pricing (we do store token usage separately for prompt-generation APIs).

Packaging & discounts
- Quarterly prepay / committed volume: standard discounts start at 15% for 12M+ monthly vectors, 25% for 50M+ (negotiable for >100M).
- We can offer a blended rate if you plan to mix dims/models across a route.

Model support and routing
- Hosted supports multiple embedding models; you can pin a route to a specific model or use routing rules to pick by traffic/latency.
- For mixed workloads we typically recommend rwd-embed-1 for lightweight embeddings and rwd-embed-large for dense vectors used for high-precision semantic search.

Next steps
- I’ll loop in Ben to map discount tiers to a sample cost table for your 20M/month projection and to outline a simple mutual action plan if you want committed pricing.

Best,
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@dataforge.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question on embeddings pricing and supported dims

Emma — quick follow-up from our side with concrete numbers tied to your 20M/month forecast.

Scenario A — No commitment (baseline)
- 1536-dim: $0.0006 * 20M = $12,000/month
- 4096-dim: $0.0018 * 20M = $36,000/month

Scenario B — Quarterly prepay, 20M/month commit (12% discount)
- 1536-dim effective: $0.000528 * 20M = $10,560/month
- 4096-dim effective: $0.001584 * 20M = $31,680/month

Blended option (mix 80% small / 20% large)
- Blended baseline: (0.8 * 0.0006 + 0.2 * 0.0018) = $0.00084 per vector → $16,800/month
- Blended prepay (12%): $14,784/month

Other notes
- We can provide a sample SSO + VPC allowlisting in the contract for enterprise-grade access.
- I attached our short ratecard and a one-pager on model compatibility. If you have an internal cost model (spreadsheet), send it over and we’ll fill the expected Redwood line items.

Attachments: RBwd-Embeddings-Quicksheet-v2.pdf

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Emma Lowe <emma@dataforge.com>

Thanks Ben/Markus — this is exactly what we needed. I’ve shared the internal cost spreadsheet (DataForge-MVP-Specs.xlsx) in the Drive link and dropped a couple of notes:

- We’ll likely start with the 1536 model for the discovery phase (high volume, lower SLO requirements) and switch a subset of routes to 4096 for improved recall on critical queries.
- Can you confirm whether the billing shows per-route breakdowns in the console (so we can attribute costs to product teams)?

If you can send a one-page mutual action plan with timelines and the 12% prepay paperwork, we’ll take it to procurement next week. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to finalize.

Best,
Emma
